headline: Perspective is the art of creating depth on flat surfaces—tricking the eye into seeing three dimensions in two
universal_truth: Representation is not reality; all models simplify what they depict
fun_facts: Linear perspective was rediscovered in the Renaissance—medieval art looks 'flat' because they hadn't mastered it
Railroad tracks seem to converge at the horizon—that's linear perspective in the real world
3D movies and VR use perspective cues to create the illusion of depth from flat screens
discussion_questions: How does perspective change how we understand an image?
What perspectives do you take for granted in how you see the world?
How does changing your 'perspective' on a problem change what you see?

hook.script: A flat canvas can show a road stretching to the horizon, buildings receding into distance, a room you could walk into. This is perspective—the technique of creating depth on flat surfaces. It's an optical illusion so convincing we forget it's a trick.

cliff.script: Medieval paintings look flat—figures float without depth. Renaissance paintings suddenly look three-dimensional. What changed? Artists discovered the mathematics of perspective.

options.text: Objects are drawn smaller as they recede, and parallel lines converge toward vanishing points—mimicking how our eyes actually see
options.response: Yes. Our eyes see distant things as smaller and parallel lines converging. Perspective replicates these visual cues on flat surfaces, tricking the brain into perceiving depth.

options.text: Shading and shadows make things look three-dimensional
options.response: Shading helps, but linear perspective's converging lines are the main depth creator...

fact1.title: Vanishing Points
fact1.script: Parallel lines in reality converge at a 'vanishing point' on the horizon in perspective drawings. Railroad tracks meet in the distance. Building edges angle toward a single point. This mathematical trick creates convincing depth.

fact2.title: Renaissance Revolution
fact2.script: Brunelleschi demonstrated perspective in 1415. Suddenly artists could create realistic space. It was a technology—a technique that had to be discovered and taught. Art before and after perspective looks radically different.

fact3.title: Perspective Everywhere
fact3.script: Video games, movies, VR all use perspective. When you see a 3D world on a flat screen, perspective cues convince your brain. The same principles from Renaissance painting drive modern entertainment.

wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: Representation is not reality. Perspective teaches that all models simplify what they depict. The map is not the territory; the picture is not the scene. Useful representations are still approximations.

outro.script: That's Day 176. Tomorrow, we'll explore how things feel to touch—texture. Until then, notice perspective in images around you—photos, screens, art—and appreciate the illusion.

growTrack.title: Perspective Shift - See Differently
growTrack.activity: Take a problem or situation and describe it from three different perspectives: yours, someone else involved, an outside observer. How does changing the 'vanishing point' change what you see? Multiple perspectives reveal what single viewpoints miss.
